raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

HiSparse's resident prefill conversion lazily gathers a batch-ordered copy of the residency table inside the layer-0 conversion. The gather is queued after `logical_topk_ready`, but the side-stream converter waits only on that event, so it can read the table before it's written.

This PR removes the gathered table. The sparse-MLA index remap kernel gets an optional `idx_mapping` indirection, off for other callers, and HiSparse passes its persistent residency table plus `request_state_indices` directly. Both are written before the forward, so the existing event orders them. Residency is stored group-major, so each group's view is a contiguous table.

Alternative to #62401, which keeps the gather and adds a layer-0 `wait_stream`.

## Test Result

- `test_hisparse_resident_prefill_reads_residency_by_state_row` reproduces the race: it fails on main (3/3 runs) and passes here.
- HiSparse unit and e2e tests pass.
- With JIT monitoring on, the new variant is never compiled after warmup.

**End to end:** GLM-5.3-NVFP4, 8×B200 TP8, HiSparse, mean of 2 reps, change vs main. Greedy outputs are byte-identical.

| workload | c | output tok/s | mean TTFT | mean TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16k in / 1k out | 16 | −0.2% | −0.3% | +0.5% |
| 16k in / 1k out | 64 | +0.0% | +1.1% | −0.4% |
| 4k in / 64 out | 16 | +1.3% | −0.3% | −2.4% |
| 4k in / 64 out | 64 | +0.1% | −0.1% | −0.1% |

**Kernel:** speedup vs main for the HiSparse conversion. H200, top-k 2048, 256 max requests, 61 resident groups, CUDA graph timing. Other sparse-MLA callers are unchanged (0.94–1.09× across the sweep).

| query tokens | 512 pages | 2048 pages | 8192 pages |
|---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 1 | 2.08× | 2.25× | 2.86× |
| 128 | 2.02× | 2.15× | 2.52× |
| 1024 | 1.33× | 1.35× | 1.53× |
| 8192 | 1.02× | 1.02× | 1.06× |
| 16384 | 0.98× | 0.98× | 1.01× |
| 32768 | 0.98× | 0.97× | 0.99× |

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```sh
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py -k "hisparse or index_group or sparse_mqa or convert or remap or residency"
pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py

vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --max-model-len <ISL+OSL+1024> \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":128}}'
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len {16384|4096} --random-output-len {1024|64} \
  --num-prompts {2c|4c} --max-concurrency c --ignore-eos --seed 42
```
</details>
